summary: Patch fixes the migrate symptom by flushing after every OutputWrapper.write(), but takes the wrong approach: the actual bug is that OutputWrapper.flush() is a TextIOBase no-op (never delegates to self._out), and forcing a flush on every write introduces a real performance regression for high-volume commands. Django's accepted fix overrides flush() instead.

issues.description: Wrong abstraction. Root cause is OutputWrapper inheriting TextIOBase.flush() (a no-op) which shadows delegation to self._out, so explicit self.stdout.flush() calls do nothing. Correct fix overrides flush() to call self._out.flush(); flushing inside write() instead is heavy-handed and side-steps the actual defect.

Reported issue title is 'flush() ... doesn't work'. This patch never makes the flush() method itself work — explicit self.stdout.flush()/self.stderr.flush() calls remain TextIOBase no-ops. Only the migrate progressive-output symptom is patched, not the named API.

Unconditional self._out.flush() on every write penalizes high-throughput commands (e.g. dumpdata writing many records to a redirected file/pipe), turning block-buffered output into per-write flushes. Avoidable inefficiency that the flush()-override approach does not incur.
No guard for streams lacking flush(); a custom self._out without a working flush could raise, where the safer fix uses hasattr(self._out, 'flush').
